Fastidious

/fa-STID-ee-us/ — stress on STID · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is fastidious pays extremely close attention to small details and insists that things be done exactly right.

A fastidious eater, the cat sniffed each new food three times before tasting.

Worked Example

The fastidious restaurant owner tasted every dish before serving it to guests, rejecting anything below his standards.

Fastidious captures not just care but a picky, high-standard attitude — a disdain for anything imperfect. It suggests someone with refined taste who rejects mediocrity, not just someone careful.

How Fastidious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

picky

picky: choosing very selectively; hard to satisfy

fussy

fussy: bothered by small flaws others would ignore

demanding

demanding: insisting that exact, high standards be met

Antonyms

easygoing

easygoing: relaxed and satisfied with almost anything

indiscriminate

indiscriminate: accepting anything without judging its quality first

How Strong Is It? — sloppy → tolerant → particular → fastidious

sloppy vs. fastidious

sloppy vs. fastidious: Sloppy is the extreme opposite of fastidious: a sloppy person ignores standards completely, while a fastidious one insists that everything meet exact standards.

tolerant vs. fastidious

tolerant vs. fastidious: Tolerant is much weaker than fastidious: a tolerant eater accepts most dishes without complaint, while a fastidious eater rejects anything that is not exactly right.

particular vs. fastidious

particular vs. fastidious: Particular is close to fastidious but milder: a particular person has clear preferences, while a fastidious one is so exacting that little ever satisfies them.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fastidi-

Root — fastidi-: loathing, squeamish distaste, excessive nicety (Latin)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: From Latin fastidium, 'loathing or squeamish distaste,' plus -ous, 'full of': a fastidious person is so full of distaste for anything imperfect that only things done exactly right will satisfy them.

Use the root in a new word: furious

Use the root in a new word: furious: Furious means 'full of fury' — the same -ous ending that makes fastidious mean 'full of squeamish distaste' for anything that falls short of exact standards.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Fastidious is the word for someone who is not just careful but picky — someone with refined taste who finds imperfection genuinely distasteful. It suggests a personality that insists on high standards. Use it when the person's pickiness comes from taste and standards, not just caution.
